Build a directed graph from a 2D elevation array for pathfinding.

Each pixel becomes a node with coordinates (i, j). Edges connect to neighboring pixels with weights based on physical distance and elevation cost.

Edge weight formula depends on cost_model

elevation: distance_m * (1 + weight * normalized_elevation) distance: distance_m slope_uphill: distance_m * (1 + weight * max(0, delta_elev) / elev_range) energy: distance_m + weight * max(0, delta_elev) absolute_elevation: distance_m * (1 + weight * normalized_abs_elevation)

where distance_m is 30m for cardinal directions, 30*sqrt(2) for diagonals.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION elevation

2D elevation array (not normalized).

TYPE: ndarray

weight

Multiplier for elevation cost (higher = prefer flat paths).

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

diagonal_movement

'always' for 8-connectivity, 'never' for 4-connectivity.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'always'

cost_model

edge cost model name.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: 'elevation'

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DiGraph

NetworkX DiGraph with nodes at (i, j) and weighted edges to neighbors.

@_log_timing
def build_graph_from_elevation(
    elevation: np.ndarray,
    weight: float = 1.0,
    diagonal_movement: str = "always",
    cost_model: str = "elevation",
) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """
    Build a directed graph from a 2D elevation array for pathfinding.

    Each pixel becomes a node with coordinates (i, j). Edges connect to
    neighboring pixels with weights based on physical distance and elevation cost.

    Edge weight formula depends on cost_model:
        elevation: distance_m * (1 + weight * normalized_elevation)
        distance:  distance_m
        slope_uphill: distance_m * (1 + weight * max(0, delta_elev) / elev_range)
        energy:    distance_m + weight * max(0, delta_elev)
        absolute_elevation: distance_m * (1 + weight * normalized_abs_elevation)
    where distance_m is 30m for cardinal directions, 30*sqrt(2) for diagonals.

    Args:
        elevation: 2D elevation array (not normalized).
        weight: Multiplier for elevation cost (higher = prefer flat paths).
        diagonal_movement: 'always' for 8-connectivity, 'never' for 4-connectivity.
        cost_model: edge cost model name.

    Returns:
        NetworkX DiGraph with nodes at (i, j) and weighted edges to neighbors.
    """
    t_start = time.time()
    rows, cols = elevation.shape
    logger.debug(
        f"build_graph_from_elevation: start rows={rows}, cols={cols}, "
        f"diagonal={diagonal_movement}, cost_model={cost_model}, weight={weight}, "
        f"graph_backend=edges"
    )

    if cost_model not in COST_MODELS:
        logger.warning(f"Unknown cost_model '{cost_model}', falling back to 'elevation'")
        cost_model = "elevation"

    # Reuse cached graph topology and only update edge weights
    t_template = time.time()
    template = _get_graph_template(rows, cols, diagonal_movement)
    logger.debug(f"build_graph_from_elevation: template fetch took {time.time() - t_template:.4f}s")

    t_weights = time.time()
    weights = _compute_edge_weights(template, elevation, weight, cost_model)
    logger.debug(f"build_graph_from_elevation: weights compute took {time.time() - t_weights:.4f}s")

    if template.distance_m.size == 0:
        return template.graph

    t_update = time.time()
    template.graph.add_weighted_edges_from(
        (
            (int(template.src_i[k]), int(template.src_j[k])),
            (int(template.dst_i[k]), int(template.dst_j[k])),
            float(weights[k]),
        )
        for k in range(len(template.src_i))
    )
    logger.debug(f"build_graph_from_elevation: edge weights update took {time.time() - t_update:.4f}s")
    logger.debug(f"build_graph_from_elevation: total time {time.time() - t_start:.4f}s")
    return template.graph

def check_path_collision(path: list[tuple[int, int]], obstacles_mask: np.ndarray) -> bool:
    """
    Check if a path crosses any obstacles in the provided mask.

    Args:
        path: List of (row, col) tuples representing the path.
        obstacles_mask: 2D numpy array where 1 indicates an obstacle and 0 indicates free space.

    Returns:
        True if any point on the path coincides with an obstacle, False otherwise.
    """
    if not path or obstacles_mask is None:
        return False

    # Attempt fast vectorized path check for common case: sequence of (row, col)
    try:
        arr = np.asarray(path)
        # If object array of tuples/lists, stack into numeric 2D array
        if arr.dtype == np.object_ and arr.ndim == 1:
            arr = np.vstack(arr)
        if arr.ndim == 2 and arr.shape[1] >= 2:
            rows = arr[:, 0].astype(np.intp)
            cols = arr[:, 1].astype(np.intp)
            # Keep only in-bounds points
            valid = (rows >= 0) & (rows < obstacles_mask.shape[0]) & (cols >= 0) & (cols < obstacles_mask.shape[1])
            if not np.any(valid):
                return False
            rows = rows[valid]
            cols = cols[valid]
            # Advanced indexing returns obstacle values for each point
            return bool(np.any(obstacles_mask[rows, cols] != 0))
    except Exception:
        # Fall through to safe scalar fallback on any error
        pass

    # Fallback: robust scalar check (handles objects with attributes, etc.)
    for p in path:
        try:
            i, j = int(p[0]), int(p[1])
        except Exception:
            try:
                i, j = int(p.y), int(p.x)  # support node-like objects if present
            except Exception:
                continue
        if 0 <= i < obstacles_mask.shape[0] and 0 <= j < obstacles_mask.shape[1]:
            if obstacles_mask[i, j] != 0:
                return True
    return False

docs.text:
Obstacle utilities: superellipse mask generation.

This module implements a small helper to create a binary mask for a rotated superellipse (Lamé curve) given parameters. It documents the meaning of n and provides a reliable implementation that accepts angles in degrees or radians.

Superellipse equation (centered coordinates): (|x|/a)^n + (|y|/b)^n <= 1

Notes about n: - n = 2.0 -> ellipse (circle when a == b) - n < 2 -> "diamond"/pointed shapes (n = 1 -> diamond / rhombus) - n > 2 -> squarer shapes; as n -> large the curve approaches a rectangle - n must be > 0.0 to produce a closed shape

The function here keeps the implementation small and deterministic so it can be used in tests and notebooks. Higher-level obstacle-generation routines can sample n from the configuration to create varied collections of shapes.

def superellipse_mask(
    shape: Tuple[int, int],
    center: Tuple[float, float],
    a: float,
    b: float,
    n: float,
    angle: float = 0.0,
    angle_degrees: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a boolean mask of a rotated superellipse.

    Args:
        shape: (rows, cols) of the output mask.
        center: (y, x) center coordinates in pixel space (can be floats).
        a: semi-axis in x-direction (pixels). Must be > 0.
        b: semi-axis in y-direction (pixels). Must be > 0.
        n: superellipse exponent. Must be > 0. Larger values -> closer to rectangle.
        angle: rotation angle in degrees if ``angle_degrees`` is True, otherwise radians.
        angle_degrees: interpret ``angle`` as degrees when True.

    Returns:
        Boolean NumPy array with True inside the superellipse and False elsewhere.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if parameters are invalid (non-positive a/b/n or shape not 2-tuple).
    """
    if len(shape) != 2:
        raise ValueError("shape must be (rows, cols)")
    rows, cols = int(shape[0]), int(shape[1])

    if a <= 0 or b <= 0:
        raise ValueError("semi-axes 'a' and 'b' must be positive numbers")
    if n <= 0:
        raise ValueError("exponent 'n' must be positive")

    if angle_degrees:
        theta = float(np.deg2rad(angle))
    else:
        theta = float(angle)

    cos_a = np.cos(theta)
    sin_a = np.sin(theta)

    # grid of coordinates centered at (center_y, center_x)
    ys = np.arange(rows, dtype=np.float64) - float(center[0])
    xs = np.arange(cols, dtype=np.float64) - float(center[1])
    y_grid, x_grid = np.meshgrid(ys, xs, indexing="ij")

    # rotate coordinates by -theta (so angle is orientation of major axis)
    xr = cos_a * x_grid + sin_a * y_grid
    yr = -sin_a * x_grid + cos_a * y_grid

    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        val = (np.abs(xr) / float(a)) ** float(n) + (np.abs(yr) / float(b)) ** float(n)

    mask = val <= 1.0
    mask = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)
    return mask

def sample_n_from_config(obstacles_cfg: dict, rng: np.random.Generator) -> float:
    """Sample superellipse exponent `n` from configuration.

    Supports the following distribution types in `obstacles_cfg['shape']['n']['distribution']`:
      - 'uniform'      : uniform between n_min and n_max
      - 'log_uniform'  : uniform in log-space between n_min and n_max
      - 'beta'         : beta distribution (a,b) scaled to [n_min, n_max]

    Backward compatibility: if the nested `shape.n` structure is missing, fall back to
    `obstacles_cfg['n_min']`, `obstacles_cfg['n_max']`, and `obstacles_cfg['n_distribution']`.
    """
    shape_cfg = obstacles_cfg.get("shape", {}) or {}
    n_cfg = shape_cfg.get("n", {}) or {}
    if not n_cfg:
        # Backward compatibility
        n_cfg = {
            "min": obstacles_cfg.get("n_min", 2.0),
            "max": obstacles_cfg.get("n_max", 100.0),
            "distribution": obstacles_cfg.get("n_distribution", {}) or {},
        }

    n_min = float(n_cfg.get("min", 2.0))
    n_max = float(n_cfg.get("max", 100.0))
    if n_min <= 0 or n_max < n_min:
        raise ValueError("Invalid n_min/n_max in obstacles config")

    dist_cfg = n_cfg.get("distribution", {}) or {}
    dist_type = str(dist_cfg.get("type", "log_uniform")).lower()

    if dist_type == "uniform":
        return float(rng.uniform(n_min, n_max))
    if dist_type == "log_uniform":
        return float(np.exp(rng.uniform(np.log(n_min), np.log(n_max))))
    # Exponential distribution on [n_min, n_max] (parameterized by rate 'lambda' > 0).
    # Sampling is performed on a truncated exponential in [0,1] and then scaled to [n_min,n_max].
    if dist_type == "exponential":
        lam = float(dist_cfg.get("lambda", dist_cfg.get("rate", 1.0)))
        if lam <= 0:
            # Invalid parameter -> fallback to uniform
            return float(rng.uniform(n_min, n_max))
        # Sample u ~ Uniform(0,1) and invert truncated exponential CDF on [0,1]:
        # CDF_trunc(s) = (1 - exp(-lam * s)) / (1 - exp(-lam)), s in [0,1]
        u = float(rng.random())
        c = 1.0 - math.exp(-lam)
        s = -(1.0 / lam) * math.log(1.0 - u * c)
        s = min(max(s, 0.0), 1.0)
        return float(n_min + s * (n_max - n_min))
    # beta distribution (default)
    if dist_type == "beta":
        a = float(dist_cfg.get("a", 2.0))
        b = float(dist_cfg.get("b", 5.0))
        # clamp to sensible positive values
        a = max(0.01, a)
        b = max(0.01, b)
        u = float(rng.beta(a, b))
        return float(n_min + u * (n_max - n_min))

    # fallback to uniform
    return float(rng.uniform(n_min, n_max))

def run_calibrate(
    outputs_dirpath: str,
    tiles_dirpath: str,
    *,
    resume: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    num_cpus: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Scan all DSM tiles to find global min/max elevation values.

    Args:
        outputs_dirpath: Directory path for output files.
        tiles_dirpath: Directory containing DSM tiles.
        resume: If True, resume from existing `outputs/calibrate/calibrate.json` and skip tiles already processed.
                If False, do not resume; will not overwrite existing `calibrate.json` unless `overwrite=True`.
        overwrite: If True and resume=False, overwrite any existing `calibrate.json` with new results.
        num_cpus: Number of CPUs to use (None means use all available CPUs, 0 disables multiprocessing).
    """
    outputs_path = Path(outputs_dirpath)

    # When tests are running (pytest sets PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST), avoid writing into the
    # repository's default `outputs/calibrate` directory and use a temp location instead.
    if os.getenv("PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST") and outputs_path.resolve() == Path("outputs/calibrate").resolve():
        tmp_base = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "passage_test_outputs" / f"calibrate_{os.getpid()}"
        logger.info("Detected pytest environment: redirecting calibrate outputs to %s", tmp_base)
        outputs_path = tmp_base

    outputs_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    tiles_path = Path(tiles_dirpath)

    if not tiles_path.exists():
        logger.error(f"Tiles directory not found: {tiles_path}")
        return

    # Discover all DSM tiles
    logger.info(f"Scanning for DSM tiles in {tiles_path}...")
    tile_files = list(tiles_path.glob("*_DSM.tif"))

    if not tile_files:
        logger.error(f"No DSM tiles found in {tiles_path}")
        return

    logger.info(f"Found {len(tile_files)} DSM tiles")

    # Harmonized startup log
    cpus = num_cpus if num_cpus is not None else os.cpu_count()
    logger.info(f"Starting calibrate: outputs={outputs_path}, tiles={tiles_path}, cpus={cpus}, resume={resume}")

    # Track global min/max
    global_min = float("inf")
    global_max = float("-inf")
    tiles_processed = 0
    tiles_failed = 0

    # Per-tile stats for detailed output
    tile_stats: list[dict] = []

    # Track failed tile filenames for debugging
    failed_tiles: list[str] = []

    # Resume from existing calibrate.json if 'resume' is True to avoid reprocessing tiles
    calibrate_json = outputs_path / "calibrate.json"
    processed_filenames: set[str] = set()
    if resume and calibrate_json.exists():
        try:
            with open(calibrate_json) as f:
                existing = json.load(f)
            existing_stats = existing.get("tile_stats", [])
            for e in existing_stats:
                fname = e.get("filename")
                if fname and e.get("min") is not None and e.get("max") is not None:
                    tile_stats.append(e)
                    processed_filenames.add(fname)
                    tiles_processed += 1
                    try:
                        global_min = min(global_min, float(e["min"]))
                        global_max = max(global_max, float(e["max"]))
                    except Exception:
                        pass
            logger.info(f"Loaded {len(processed_filenames)} existing tile stats from {calibrate_json}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to load existing calibrate.json: {e}")
    else:
        if calibrate_json.exists() and not resume and not overwrite:
            logger.info(
                "Existing calibrate.json present and resume=False; not overwriting (set overwrite=True to force)"
            )
            return
        if calibrate_json.exists() and not resume and overwrite:
            logger.info("--overwrite specified: existing calibrate.json will be recomputed")

    # Filter out already-processed tiles (if any)
    remaining_tile_files = [tf for tf in tile_files if tf.name not in processed_filenames]
    if not remaining_tile_files:
        logger.info("All tiles already processed, skipping processing step")
    else:
        # Processing using optional multiprocessing
        # num_cpus semantics: None => use all CPUs, 0 => sequential, N => use N cores
        if num_cpus == 0:
            # Sequential processing
            for tile_file in tqdm(remaining_tile_files, desc="Processing tiles"):
                name, tmin, tmax, err = _process_tile_worker(tile_file)
                if err is None:
                    tile_stats.append({"filename": name, "min": tmin, "max": tmax})
                    global_min = min(global_min, tmin)
                    global_max = max(global_max, tmax)
                    tiles_processed += 1
                else:
                    if err == "no_valid_data":
                        logger.warning(f"No valid data in tile {name}")
                    else:
                        logger.warning(f"Failed to process tile {name}: {err}")
                    tiles_failed += 1
                    failed_tiles.append(name)
        else:
            pool_size = num_cpus if num_cpus is not None else os.cpu_count()
            logger.info(f"Running calibration with {pool_size} worker processes")
            try:
                # Multiprocessing branch is hard to exercise under test harness; exclude from coverage.
                with multiprocessing.Pool(pool_size) as pool:  # pragma: no cover
                    for name, tmin, tmax, err in tqdm(
                        pool.imap_unordered(_process_tile_worker, remaining_tile_files),
                        total=len(remaining_tile_files),
                        desc="Processing tiles",
                    ):
                        if err is None:
                            tile_stats.append({"filename": name, "min": tmin, "max": tmax})
                            global_min = min(global_min, tmin)
                            global_max = max(global_max, tmax)
                            tiles_processed += 1
                        else:
                            if err == "no_valid_data":
                                logger.warning(f"No valid data in tile {name}")
                            else:
                                logger.warning(f"Failed to process tile {name}: {err}")
                            tiles_failed += 1
                            failed_tiles.append(name)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:  # pragma: no cover
                logger.warning("Calibration interrupted by user")
                # Pool will be terminated automatically by context manager on exception

    # Check if we found any valid data
    if tiles_processed == 0:
        logger.error("No tiles were successfully processed")
        return

    # Log results
    logger.info(f"Processed {tiles_processed} tiles ({tiles_failed} failed)")
    logger.info(f"Global min elevation: {global_min}")
    logger.info(f"Global max elevation: {global_max}")

    # Enrich tile_stats with parsed lat/lon and build max elevation image
    def _parse_lat_lon_from_filename(filename: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
        pattern = r"([NS])(\d{3})([EW])(\d{3})"
        m = re.search(pattern, filename)
        if not m:
            return None
        lat_char, lat_val, lon_char, lon_val = m.groups()
        lat = int(lat_val) * (-1 if lat_char == "S" else 1)
        lon = int(lon_val) * (-1 if lon_char == "W" else 1)
        return lat, lon

    # Create an image with lat from -90..90 and lon from 0..180 -> size (181 x 181)
    LAT_MIN = -90
    LAT_MAX = 90
    LON_MIN = -180
    LON_MAX = 180
    LAT_STEPS = LAT_MAX - LAT_MIN + 1
    LON_STEPS = LON_MAX - LON_MIN + 1

    # Initialize RGB image (BGR for OpenCV)
    max_map = np.zeros((LAT_STEPS, LON_STEPS, 3), dtype=np.uint8)  # initialized to black

    # Update tile_stats entries to include lat/lon
    updated_tile_stats: list[dict] = []
    for entry in tile_stats:
        filename = entry.get("filename")
        coords = _parse_lat_lon_from_filename(filename)
        if coords is None:
            updated_tile_stats.append({**entry})
            continue
        lat, lon = coords
        entry_with_coords = {**entry, "lat": lat, "lon": lon}
        updated_tile_stats.append(entry_with_coords)

        # Only map tiles with lon in [0,180]
        if entry.get("max") is None:
            continue
        if lon < LON_MIN or lon > LON_MAX:
            continue
        if lat < LAT_MIN or lat > LAT_MAX:
            continue

        # Map to pixel coordinates
        x_idx = lon - LON_MIN  # 0..LON_STEPS-1
        y_idx = LAT_MAX - lat  # lat 90 -> y 0; lat -90 -> y LAT_STEPS-1

        # Normalize elevation value between global_min and global_max
        if global_max > global_min:
            v = (entry["max"] - global_min) / (global_max - global_min)
            v = max(0.0, min(1.0, v))
        else:
            v = 0.0

        # Color mapping: use standard 'terrain' colormap from matplotlib
        rgba = cm.get_cmap("terrain")(v)
        r = int(rgba[0] * 255)
        g = int(rgba[1] * 255)
        b = int(rgba[2] * 255)
        max_map[y_idx, x_idx] = (b, g, r)

    # Filter out any entries that failed (missing min or max) before saving
    final_tile_stats = [e for e in updated_tile_stats if e.get("min") is not None and e.get("max") is not None]
    excluded_count = len(updated_tile_stats) - len(final_tile_stats)
    if excluded_count > 0:
        logger.info(f"Excluded {excluded_count} failed/incomplete tile entries from output JSON")

    # Save results
    results = {
        "global_min": global_min,
        "global_max": global_max,
        "tiles_processed": tiles_processed,
        "tiles_failed": tiles_failed,
        "failed_tiles": failed_tiles,
        "tiles_dirpath": str(tiles_path),
        "tile_stats": final_tile_stats,
    }

    json_path = outputs_path / "calibrate.json"
    with open(json_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

    # Save map image
    map_path = outputs_path / "max_elevation_map.png"
    try:
        cv2.imwrite(str(map_path), max_map)
        logger.info(f"Max elevation map saved to {map_path}")
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
        logger.error(f"Failed to save max elevation map: {e}")

    # Create peak-to-peak (max-min) map and save it
    # Gather ptp values
    ptp_values = []
    ptp_entries: list[tuple[int, int, float]] = []  # (lat, lon, ptp)
    for entry in final_tile_stats:
        amin = entry.get("min")
        amax = entry.get("max")
        lat = entry.get("lat")
        lon = entry.get("lon")
        if amin is None or amax is None or lat is None or lon is None:
            continue
        if lon < LON_MIN or lon > LON_MAX:
            continue
        if lat < LAT_MIN or lat > LAT_MAX:
            continue
        ptp = float(amax) - float(amin)
        ptp_values.append(ptp)
        ptp_entries.append((lat, lon, ptp))

    ptp_map = np.zeros((LAT_STEPS, LON_STEPS, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

    if ptp_values:
        ptp_min = min(ptp_values)
        ptp_max = max(ptp_values)
        for lat, lon, ptp in ptp_entries:
            x_idx = int(lon - LON_MIN)
            y_idx = int(LAT_MAX - lat)
            if ptp_max > ptp_min:
                v = (ptp - ptp_min) / (ptp_max - ptp_min)
                v = max(0.0, min(1.0, v))
            else:
                v = 0.0
            rgba = cm.get_cmap("plasma")(v)
            r = int(rgba[0] * 255)
            g = int(rgba[1] * 255)
            b = int(rgba[2] * 255)
            ptp_map[y_idx, x_idx] = (b, g, r)

        ptp_path = outputs_path / "ptp_elevation_map.png"
        try:
            cv2.imwrite(str(ptp_path), ptp_map)
            logger.info(f"PTP elevation map saved to {ptp_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to save PTP elevation map: {e}")

        # Add ptp summary to results
        results["ptp_min"] = float(ptp_min)
        results["ptp_max"] = float(ptp_max)
    else:
        logger.info("No PTP values found; skipping PTP map generation")

    logger.info(f"Calibration results saved to {json_path}")

def download_tile(args: tuple[int, int, str | None]) -> tuple[int, int, str, bool, bool]:
    """
    Check if a URL is valid for a given lat/lon pair, and download/extract if valid.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (lat_min, lon_min, raw_dir_str) coordinates.
              raw_dir_str can be None to skip download, or a path string for multiprocessing compatibility.

    Returns:
        Tuple of (lat_min, lon_min, url, url_valid, extracted).
    """
    lat_min, lon_min, raw_dir_str = args
    lat_max = lat_min + 5
    lon_max = lon_min + 5
    lat_min_char = "S" if lat_min < 0 else "N"
    lat_max_char = "S" if lat_max < 0 else "N"
    lon_min_char = "W" if lon_min < 0 else "E"
    lon_max_char = "W" if lon_max < 0 else "E"
    part1 = f"{lat_min_char}{abs(lat_min):03d}{lon_min_char}{abs(lon_min):03d}"
    part2 = f"{lat_max_char}{abs(lat_max):03d}{lon_max_char}{abs(lon_max):03d}"
    filename = f"{part1}_{part2}.zip"
    url = f"https://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/aw3d30/data/release_v2404/{filename}"

    try:
        response = requests.head(url, timeout=1)
        status_code = response.status_code
        url_valid = status_code == HTTP_STATUS_OK
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException:
        url_valid = False

    extracted = False

    # Download and extract if valid and raw_dir is provided
    if url_valid and raw_dir_str is not None:
        raw_dir = Path(raw_dir_str)
        try:
            zip_path = raw_dir / "archives" / filename
            zip_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # extract_folder = raw_dir / "extracted"
            # extract_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            files_folder = raw_dir / "tiles"
            files_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

            # Download the file once
            response = requests.get(url, timeout=180, stream=True)
            if response.status_code == HTTP_STATUS_OK:
                with open(zip_path, "wb") as f:
                    for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
                        f.write(chunk)

                # Extract only *_DSM.tif entries into files_folder without extracting whole archive
                try:
                    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "r") as zip_ref:
                        members = [m for m in zip_ref.namelist() if m.upper().endswith("_DSM.TIF")]
                        if members:
                            count = 0
                            for member in members:
                                filename_member = os.path.basename(member)
                                if not filename_member:
                                    continue
                                dest_path = files_folder / filename_member
                                try:
                                    with zip_ref.open(member) as src, open(dest_path, "wb") as dst:
                                        shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst)
                                    count += 1
                                except Exception as e:
                                    logger.warning(f"Failed copying DSM file {member} to {dest_path}: {e}")
                            if count > 0:
                                extracted = True
                                logger.info(f"Copied {count} _DSM.tif files from {zip_path.name} to {files_folder}")
                        else:
                            logger.info(f"No _DSM.tif files found in archive {zip_path.name}")
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"Failed to extract DSM files from archive {zip_path}: {e}")

                # Cleanup: remove zip file
                try:
                    zip_path.unlink()
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning(f"Could not remove zip file {zip_path}: {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to download or extract tile for {lat_min}, {lon_min}: {e}")
            pass  # Continue even if download fails, we still return validity

    return (lat_min, lon_min, url, url_valid, extracted)

def generate_status_map(df_results: pd.DataFrame, output_path: Path) -> None:
    """
    Generate a PNG visualization of URL status.

    Args:
        df_results: DataFrame with lat_min, lon_min, url, url_valid columns.
        output_path: Path to save the PNG file.
    """
    logger.info("Generating status map image...")

    # Define geographic parameters
    MIN_LAT_DATA = -90
    MAX_LAT_DATA = 85
    MIN_LON_DATA = -180
    MAX_LON_DATA = 175
    LAT_STEP = 5
    LON_STEP = 5

    NUM_LAT_STEPS = int((MAX_LAT_DATA - MIN_LAT_DATA) / LAT_STEP) + 1
    NUM_LON_STEPS = int((MAX_LON_DATA - MIN_LON_DATA) / LON_STEP) + 1

    CELL_SIZE = 10  # Size of each cell in pixels
    IMG_HEIGHT = NUM_LAT_STEPS * CELL_SIZE
    IMG_WIDTH = NUM_LON_STEPS * CELL_SIZE

    # Create a blank image (black background). OpenCV uses BGR color format.
    image = np.zeros((IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

    COLOR_WHITE_BGR = (255, 255, 255)  # Valid URL (White)
    COLOR_BLACK_BGR = (0, 0, 0)  # Invalid URL (Black)

    if not df_results.empty:
        for _index, row in df_results.iterrows():
            lat_min = row["lat_min"]
            lon_min = row["lon_min"]
            url_valid = row["url_valid"]

            # Normalize latitude to y-index: higher latitudes (north) at smaller y (top)
            y_idx = int((MAX_LAT_DATA - lat_min) / LAT_STEP)

            # Normalize longitude to x-index: lower longitudes (west) at smaller x (left)
            x_idx = int((lon_min - MIN_LON_DATA) / LON_STEP)

            color = COLOR_WHITE_BGR if url_valid else COLOR_BLACK_BGR

            # Calculate pixel coordinates for the top-left corner of the cell
            y1 = y_idx * CELL_SIZE
            x1 = x_idx * CELL_SIZE

            # Assign color to the pixels in the cell
            if 0 <= y1 < IMG_HEIGHT and 0 <= x1 < IMG_WIDTH:
                y2 = min(y1 + CELL_SIZE, IMG_HEIGHT)
                x2 = min(x1 + CELL_SIZE, IMG_WIDTH)
                image[y1:y2, x1:x2] = color
            else:
                logger.warning(
                    f"Calculated cell indices ({y_idx}, {x_idx}) "
                    f"for lat/lon ({lat_min}, {lon_min}) are out of "
                    "expected image bounds. Skipping."
                )
    else:
        logger.warning("DataFrame is empty. Cannot generate status map image.")

    try:
        cv2.imwrite(str(output_path), image)
        logger.info(f"Status map image saved to {output_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to save image {output_path}: {e}")

def run_download(outputs_dirpath: str, *, resume: bool = True, num_cpus: int | None = None) -> None:
    """
    Main orchestration function for downloading and tracking tile availability.

    Args:
        outputs_dirpath: Directory path for output files.
        resume: If True, resume from existing CSV file, skipping already-checked pairs.
        num_cpus: Number of CPUs to use for multiprocessing.
            None: use all CPUs (default)
            0: disable multiprocessing (useful for debugging)
            N: use N CPUs
    """
    outputs_path = Path(outputs_dirpath)
    outputs_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Harmonized startup log
    cpus = num_cpus if num_cpus is not None else os.cpu_count()
    logger.info(f"Starting download: outputs={outputs_path}, cpus={cpus}, resume={resume}")

    csv_path = outputs_path / "download.csv"
    png_path = outputs_path / "world_coverage.png"

    # Generate all lat/lon pairs
    all_pairs = []
    for lat_min in range(-90, 90, 5):
        for lon_min in range(-180, 180, 5):
            all_pairs.append((lat_min, lon_min))

    # Load existing results if resume is enabled
    existing_results: list[tuple[int, int, str, bool]] = []
    existing_pairs: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    existing_extracted: dict[tuple[int, int], bool] = {}

    if resume and csv_path.exists():
        logger.info(f"Resuming from existing CSV file: {csv_path}")
        try:
            df_existing = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
            logger.info(f"Loaded {len(df_existing)} existing results")
            for _, row in df_existing.iterrows():
                lat, lon = int(row["lat_min"]), int(row["lon_min"])
                extracted_flag = bool(row.get("extracted", False))
                existing_pairs.add((lat, lon))
                existing_extracted[(lat, lon)] = extracted_flag
                existing_results.append((lat, lon, row["url"], row["url_valid"], extracted_flag))
        except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, Exception) as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to load CSV: {e}. Starting fresh.")
    else:
        if csv_path.exists():
            os.unlink(csv_path)
        logger.info("Starting fresh download (no resume)")

    # Create raw directory for downloads
    raw_dir = outputs_path
    raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    raw_dir_str = str(raw_dir)

    # Filter pairs to process. If resuming, re-queue pairs whose previous 'extracted' value was False
    pairs_to_process = []
    for lat, lon in all_pairs:
        if (lat, lon) not in existing_pairs:
            pairs_to_process.append((lat, lon, raw_dir_str))
        else:
            # if previously checked but not extracted successfully, redo
            if not existing_extracted.get((lat, lon), False):
                pairs_to_process.append((lat, lon, raw_dir_str))

    if pairs_to_process:
        num_already_checked = len(existing_pairs)
        num_failed_extractions = sum(1 for v in existing_extracted.values() if not v)
        logger.info(
            f"Processing {len(pairs_to_process)} remaining pairs (skipping {num_already_checked} already checked; "
            f"reprocessing {num_failed_extractions} failed extractions)"
        )

        file_exists = csv_path.exists()
        new_results = []

        # Open CSV once and append each result as it is produced
        with open(csv_path, "a", newline="") as csvfile:
            writer = csv.writer(csvfile)
            # write header if file did not exist before
            if not file_exists:
                writer.writerow(["lat_min", "lon_min", "url", "url_valid", "extracted"])
                csvfile.flush()
                try:
                    os.fsync(csvfile.fileno())
                except Exception:
                    pass

            # Process URL checks and downloads, writing each result immediately
            if num_cpus == 0:
                # Sequential processing (useful for debugging)
                logger.info("Running in sequential mode (no multiprocessing)")
                for res in tqdm((download_tile(pair) for pair in pairs_to_process), total=len(pairs_to_process)):
                    try:
                        writer.writerow(res)
                        csvfile.flush()
                        try:
                            os.fsync(csvfile.fileno())
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                    except Exception as e:
                        logger.warning(f"Failed writing result {res} to CSV: {e}")
                    new_results.append(res)
            else:
                # Multiprocessing
                pool_size = num_cpus if num_cpus is not None else os.cpu_count()
                logger.info(f"Running with {pool_size} CPUs")
                with multiprocessing.Pool(pool_size) as pool:
                    for res in tqdm(pool.imap(download_tile, pairs_to_process), total=len(pairs_to_process)):
                        try:
                            writer.writerow(res)
                            csvfile.flush()
                            try:
                                os.fsync(csvfile.fileno())
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        except Exception as e:
                            logger.warning(f"Failed writing result {res} to CSV: {e}")
                        new_results.append(res)

        # Merge existing and new results
        all_results = existing_results + new_results
        df_results = pd.DataFrame(all_results, columns=["lat_min", "lon_min", "url", "url_valid", "extracted"])
        logger.info(f"URL status codes appended to {csv_path}")
    else:
        logger.info("All pairs already checked, nothing to process")
        df_results = pd.DataFrame(existing_results, columns=["lat_min", "lon_min", "url", "url_valid", "extracted"])

    # Generate status map
    generate_status_map(df_results, png_path)
    logger.info("Download completed.")

def parse_path_csv(csv_path: Path) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Parse a path .csv file with rows "x,y" (no header) and return [[row,col], ...]."""

    out: list[list[int]] = []
    with csv_path.open(newline="") as fh:
        reader = csv.reader(fh)
        for row in reader:
            if len(row) < 2:
                continue
            x = int(row[0].strip())
            y = int(row[1].strip())
            out.append([x, y])
    return out

def export_and_upload(
    dataset_dirpath: str | Path = "outputs/dataset",
    calibrate_dirpath: str | Path = "outputs/calibrate",
    notebooks_dirpath: str | Path = "notebooks",
    resolutions: list[int] | None = None,
    repo_id: str | None = None,
    execute_notebooks: bool = True,
    max_notebook_retries: int | None = 3,
    notebook_retry_delay: int = 5,
    env_path: str | Path | None = None,
    secret_path: str | Path | None = None,
    private: bool = False,
    create_repo: bool = True,
    skip_upload: bool = False,
    num_cpus: int | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """Export and upload datasets to Hugging Face.

    num_cpus semantics: None => use all CPUs (default); 0 => disable multiprocessing (sequential); N => use N CPUs.
    """
    cpus = num_cpus if num_cpus is not None else os.cpu_count()
    dataset_path = Path(dataset_dirpath).resolve()
    calibrate_path = Path(calibrate_dirpath).resolve()
    notebooks_path = Path(notebooks_dirpath).resolve()
    dataset_notebook = notebooks_path / "_dataset.ipynb"
    export_dirpath = calibrate_path.parent / "export"
    export_dirpath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not dataset_path.exists():
        logger.error(f"Dataset directory not found: {dataset_path}")
        return False

    config_file = notebooks_path.parent / "config" / "config.yaml"
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(config_file.read_text())
    chunk_sizes = cfg["export"]["chunk_size"]

    # Extract solver names from config
    solver_names = [solver["name"] for solver in cfg.get("solvers", [])]
    if not solver_names:
        logger.error("No solvers defined in config.yaml")
        return False

    if resolutions is None:
        resolutions = sorted([int(d.name) for d in dataset_path.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and d.name.isdigit()])

    split_names = ["train", "calibration", "validation", "test"]

    # if skip_upload:
    #     logger.info("Skipping upload as requested; notebooks (if any) executed")
    #     return True

    # TODO: extract getting username and repo_name from env to a separate function
    username, repo_name, token = _load_hf_credentials(
        env_path=Path(env_path) if env_path else None,
        secret_path=Path(secret_path) if secret_path else None,
    )
    if repo_id is None:
        repo_id = f"{username}/{repo_name}"

    if True:
        assets_readme_path = notebooks_path.parent / "assets" / "README.md"
        readme_text = _load_and_customize_readme(
            assets_readme_path, repo_id, resolutions, split_names, cfg["export"]["default"], solver_names
        )
        with open(export_dirpath / "README.md", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(readme_text)

        (export_dirpath / "assets").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for image_filepath in (notebooks_path.parent / "assets").glob("*.png"):
            shutil.copy2(
                str(image_filepath.resolve()), str((export_dirpath / "assets" / image_filepath.name).resolve())
            )

        (export_dirpath / "calibration").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for filepath in calibrate_path.glob("*"):
            if ".bak" in filepath.name:
                continue
            shutil.copy2(
                str(filepath.resolve()),
                str((export_dirpath / "calibration" / filepath.name).resolve()),
            )

        for res in resolutions:
            for sample in [True, False]:
                config_name = _config_name(res, sample)
                res_dir = dataset_path / str(res)
                if not res_dir.exists():
                    continue

                # split_datasets: dict[str, Dataset] = {}
                for split in split_names:
                    split_dir = res_dir / split
                    if not split_dir.exists():
                        continue
                    export_path = export_dirpath / config_name / split
                    export_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    metadata_root = split_dir / "metadata"
                    metadata_filepaths = list(metadata_root.rglob("*.yaml"))
                    if len(metadata_filepaths) == 0:
                        logger.info(f"No metadata files for {config_name}/{split}; skipping")
                        continue
                    rows: list[dict] = []
                    rows_max = cfg["export"]["sample"]["num_samples"] if sample else None
                    chunk_size = chunk_sizes[res]
                    logger.info(
                        f"Processing {len(metadata_filepaths)} files for {config_name}/{split} with chunk size {chunk_size}"
                    )
                    num_chunk = 0
                    num_chunks = len(metadata_filepaths) // chunk_size + (
                        1 if len(metadata_filepaths) % chunk_size != 0 else 0
                    )

                    # Respect num_cpus semantics: 0 => sequential; N => use N CPUs (reserve 1 for system by subtracting 1 where appropriate)
                    if cpus == 0:
                        logger.info(f"Running in sequential mode (no multiprocessing) for {config_name}/{split}")
                        iterable = map(
                            partial(_process_meta_for_prepare, res, sample, solver_names), metadata_filepaths
                        )
                    else:
                        pool_size = max(cpus - 1, 1)
                        logger.info(f"Running metadata processing with {pool_size} worker processes")
                        pool = mp.Pool(processes=min(pool_size, len(metadata_filepaths)))
                        iterable = pool.imap(
                            partial(_process_meta_for_prepare, res, sample, solver_names), metadata_filepaths
                        )

                    try:
                        for row in tqdm(
                            iterable,
                            total=len(metadata_filepaths),
                            desc=f"Loading metadata for {config_name}/{split}",
                            unit="file",
                        ):
                            rows.append(row)
                            if len(rows) >= chunk_size:
                                table = Dataset.from_list(rows, features=_features(sample, solver_names)).data.table
                                parquet_filepath = f"{export_path}/data-{num_chunk:05d}.parquet"
                                logger.info(
                                    f"Writing chunk {num_chunk + 1}/{num_chunks} for {config_name}/{split} with {len(rows)} rows: {parquet_filepath}"
                                )
                                pq.write_table(
                                    table,
                                    parquet_filepath,
                                    compression="zstd",
                                    compression_level=cfg["export"]["compression_level"],
                                )
                                logger.info(
                                    f"Writing chunk {num_chunk + 1}/{num_chunks} for {config_name}/{split} with {len(rows)} rows: {parquet_filepath} - done"
                                )
                                rows = []
                                num_chunk += 1
                            if rows_max is not None and len(rows) >= rows_max:
                                logger.info(
                                    f"Reached maximum sample size of {rows_max} for {config_name}/{split}; stopping load"
                                )
                                break
                    finally:
                        if cpus != 0:
                            pool.close()
                            pool.join()

                    if len(rows) > 0:
                        table = Dataset.from_list(rows, features=_features(sample, solver_names)).data.table
                        parquet_filepath = f"{export_path}/data-{num_chunk:05d}.parquet"
                        logger.info(
                            f"Writing final chunk for {config_name}/{split} with {len(rows)} rows: {parquet_filepath}"
                        )
                        pq.write_table(
                            table,
                            parquet_filepath,
                            compression="zstd",
                            compression_level=cfg["export"]["compression_level"],
                        )
                        logger.info(
                            f"Writing final chunk for {config_name}/{split} with {len(rows)} rows: {parquet_filepath} - done"
                        )
                        rows = []
                        num_chunk += 1

                if execute_notebooks and not sample:
                    output_notebook = export_dirpath / config_name / "dataset.ipynb"
                    output_notebook.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    parameters = {
                        "RESOLUTION": res,
                        "DATASET_DIRPATH": str(dataset_path),
                        "CONFIG_FILEPATH": str(config_file),
                        "CALIBRATE_FILEPATH": str(calibrate_path / "calibrate.json"),
                        "MAX_WORKERS": cpus or 8,
                    }
                    retries = None if max_notebook_retries == 0 else max_notebook_retries
                    # Pass parameters as positional arg (tests may inspect positional args)
                    _execute_notebook_with_retries(
                        dataset_notebook,
                        output_notebook,
                        parameters,
                        cwd=notebooks_path,
                        max_retries=retries,
                        retry_delay=notebook_retry_delay,
                    )

        for notebook_filepath in notebooks_path.glob("*.ipynb"):
            if notebook_filepath.name.startswith("_"):
                logger.info(f"Skipping notebook {notebook_filepath.name} (starts with '_')")
                continue
            output_notebook = export_dirpath / "notebooks" / notebook_filepath.name
            output_notebook.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # retries = None if max_notebook_retries == 0 else max_notebook_retries
            # _execute_notebook_with_retries(
            #     notebook_filepath,
            #     output_notebook,
            #     parameters={},
            #     cwd=notebooks_path,
            #     max_retries=retries,
            #     retry_delay=notebook_retry_delay,
            # )
            shutil.copy2(str(notebook_filepath.resolve()), str(output_notebook.resolve()))

    if skip_upload:
        logger.info("Skipping upload as requested; notebooks (if any) executed")
        return True

    login(token=token)
    api = HfApi()
    if create_repo:
        api.create_repo(repo_id=repo_id, repo_type="dataset", private=private, exist_ok=True)

    if cpus == 0:
        upload_workers = 1
    else:
        upload_workers = max(cpus - 1, 1)

    _reset_hf_upload_cache(export_dirpath)
    api.upload_large_folder(
        repo_id=repo_id,
        repo_type="dataset",
        folder_path=str(export_dirpath.resolve()),
        num_workers=upload_workers,
        ignore_patterns=["*.ipynb_checkpoints"],
    )

    logger.info(f"✓ Export complete: https://huggingface.co/datasets/{repo_id}")
    return True

def encode_tensor_blob(arr: np.ndarray, level: int = TENSOR_COMPRESSION_LEVEL) -> bytes:
    """Encode a numpy array as zstd-compressed raw bytes.

    Args:
        arr: Numpy array to encode.
        level: Zstd compression level (1-22, default 3).

    Returns:
        Compressed bytes blob.
    """
    arr = np.ascontiguousarray(arr)
    c = zstd.ZstdCompressor(level=level)
    return c.compress(arr.tobytes())

def decode_tensor_blob(blob: bytes, shape: tuple, dtype: str = "float32") -> np.ndarray:
    """Decode a zstd-compressed tensor blob back to numpy array.

    Args:
        blob: Zstd-compressed raw bytes.
        shape: Target shape for the array.
        dtype: Numpy dtype string (default 'float32').

    Returns:
        Decoded numpy array with specified shape and dtype.
    """
    d = zstd.ZstdDecompressor()
    b = d.decompress(blob)
    return np.frombuffer(b, dtype=np.dtype(dtype)).reshape(shape)

def tensor_to_image(
    tensor: np.ndarray,
    path_pixels: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None,
    alt_path_pixels: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None,
    elev_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Convert a tensor to a BGR image for visualization.

    Supports either:
        - 2-channel tensors (elevation, markers) with the path provided via
            `path_pixels` (callers should provide extracted path pixels explicitly).
        - 3-channel tensors (elevation, markers, obstacles) where the third channel is
            treated as obstacles; path pixels should still be provided via `path_pixels`.

    This function now supports drawing two paths at once for comparison:
        - `path_pixels`: primary path (drawn in yellow by default)
        - `alt_path_pixels`: secondary path (drawn in green by default)

    Color mapping and overlays:
        - Elevation -> rendered with matplotlib 'terrain' colormap (base image)
        - Markers -> highlighted (start_point lime, end_point cyan)
        - Primary path -> yellow overlay (drawn as polyline/contours)
        - Secondary path -> green overlay (drawn as polyline/contours and drawn last on top)
        - Obstacles -> red overlay (drawn before paths)

    Args:
        tensor: float32 array of shape (H, W, 2) or (H, W, 3).
        path_pixels: Optional list of (i, j) tuples indicating primary path pixels.
        alt_path_pixels: Optional list of (i, j) tuples indicating secondary path pixels.
        elev_range: Optional (min, max) tuple to use for elevation normalization. If None, tensor min/max are used.

    Returns:
        BGR image as uint8 array of shape (H, W, 3).
    """
    if tensor.ndim != 3 or tensor.shape[2] not in (2, 3):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected tensor of shape (H, W, 2) or (H, W, 3), got {tensor.shape}")

    elevation_channel = tensor[:, :, 0]
    marker_channel = tensor[:, :, 1]

    # Debug: log elevation min/max before normalization
    elev_raw_min = float(np.min(elevation_channel))
    elev_raw_max = float(np.max(elevation_channel))
    logger.debug(f"tensor_to_image: elevation BEFORE normalization: min={elev_raw_min:.4f}, max={elev_raw_max:.4f}")

    # Third channel is assumed to be obstacles by default (tensor shape 3)
    if tensor.shape[2] == 3:
        obstacles_channel = tensor[:, :, 2]
    else:
        obstacles_channel = np.zeros_like(elevation_channel, dtype=np.float32)

    # Build path channels from provided path lists (callers must provide them when relevant)
    path_channel = np.zeros_like(elevation_channel, dtype=np.float32)
    alt_path_channel = np.zeros_like(elevation_channel, dtype=np.float32)
    if path_pixels:
        for pi, pj in path_pixels:
            if 0 <= int(pi) < path_channel.shape[0] and 0 <= int(pj) < path_channel.shape[1]:
                path_channel[int(pi), int(pj)] = 1.0
    if alt_path_pixels:
        for pi, pj in alt_path_pixels:
            if 0 <= int(pi) < alt_path_channel.shape[0] and 0 <= int(pj) < alt_path_channel.shape[1]:
                alt_path_channel[int(pi), int(pj)] = 1.0

    # Normalize elevation using provided elev_range tuple (min, max) in same units as elevation_channel
    if (
        elev_range is not None
        and isinstance(elev_range, tuple)
        and len(elev_range) == 2
        and elev_range[1] > elev_range[0]
    ):
        emn, emx = float(elev_range[0]), float(elev_range[1])
        norm = (elevation_channel - emn) / (emx - emn)
        logger.debug(f"tensor_to_image: using provided elevation range: [{emn:.1f}, {emx:.1f}]")
    else:
        e_min, e_max = elev_raw_min, elev_raw_max
        if e_max > e_min:
            norm = (elevation_channel - e_min) / (e_max - e_min)
        else:
            # If the elevation channel is constant and already in [0, 1], use it directly
            if 0.0 <= e_min <= 1.0:
                norm = elevation_channel.astype(np.float32)
            else:
                norm = np.zeros_like(elevation_channel, dtype=np.float32)

    norm = np.clip(norm, 0.0, 1.0)

    # Debug: log elevation min/max after normalization
    norm_min = float(np.min(norm))
    norm_max = float(np.max(norm))
    logger.debug(f"tensor_to_image: elevation AFTER normalization: min={norm_min:.4f}, max={norm_max:.4f}")

    # Use matplotlib 'terrain' colormap for elevation visualization (RGB)
    # If caller provided elev_range tuple, rescale using those bounds (they must be in same units as elevation_channel)
    try:
        import matplotlib as mpl

        if (
            elev_range is not None
            and isinstance(elev_range, tuple)
            and len(elev_range) == 2
            and elev_range[1] > elev_range[0]
        ):
            emn, emx = float(elev_range[0]), float(elev_range[1])
            norm_local = (elevation_channel - emn) / (emx - emn)
            norm_local = np.clip(norm_local, 0.0, 1.0)
        else:
            norm_local = norm

        # Use non-deprecated colormap access
        terrain_rgb = (mpl.colormaps.get_cmap("terrain")(norm_local)[:, :, :3] * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        # Convert RGB -> BGR for OpenCV
        img = terrain_rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()
    except Exception:
        # Fallback: grayscale elevation in Blue channel
        elev_scaled = (norm * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        img = cv2.merge([elev_scaled, elev_scaled, elev_scaled])

    # Compute obstacle mask and log counts (assignment happens after path/markers to preserve overlay priority)
    obst_mask = obstacles_channel > 0.5
    has_end = bool(np.any(marker_channel > 0.5))
    has_background = bool(np.any(marker_channel < -0.5))
    start_mask = (
        np.isclose(marker_channel, 0.0) if (has_end or has_background) else np.zeros_like(marker_channel, dtype=bool)
    )
    end_mask = marker_channel > 0.5
    logger.debug(
        "tensor_to_image: obst_count=%d, path_count=%d, start_count=%d, end_count=%d",
        int(np.sum(obst_mask)),
        int(np.sum(path_channel > 0.5)),
        int(np.sum(start_mask)),
        int(np.sum(end_mask)),
    )

    # Determine resolution and scale factors (base reference = 64)
    H, W = elevation_channel.shape
    res = max(H, W)
    base = 64
    scale = float(res) / float(base) if base > 0 else 1.0

    # Path thickness scales with resolution but made thinner: 1px at 64 -> round(scale * 0.5)
    path_thickness = max(1, int(round(scale * 0.5)))

    # Marker plus arm length unchanged; marker thickness reduced for thinner markers
    marker_arm = max(1, int(round(scale)))
    marker_thickness = max(1, int(round(max(1, scale * 0.25))))

    # Colors (BGR)
    obst_color = (0, 0, 255)  # red
    start_color = (255, 255, 0)  # cyan
    end_color = (255, 0, 0)  # blue
    # Primary path colors: polyline and single-pixel points are yellow (path without obstacles)
    path_poly_color = (0, 255, 255)  # yellow (B low, G high, R high)
    path_point_color = path_poly_color  # yellow for single-pixel path points
    # Alternate/with-obstacles path uses green and is drawn last on top
    alt_poly_color = (0, 255, 0)  # green

    # 1) Draw obstacles on top of elevation
    if np.any(obst_mask):
        img[obst_mask] = obst_color

    # 2) Draw start and end markers (plus-signs) without white surrounding
    start_positions = np.argwhere(start_mask)
    end_positions = np.argwhere(end_mask)
    for mi, mj in start_positions:
        cx, cy = int(mj), int(mi)  # (x, y)
        cv2.line(img, (cx - marker_arm, cy), (cx + marker_arm, cy), color=start_color, thickness=marker_thickness)
        cv2.line(img, (cx, cy - marker_arm), (cx, cy + marker_arm), color=start_color, thickness=marker_thickness)
    for mi, mj in end_positions:
        cx, cy = int(mj), int(mi)  # (x, y)
        cv2.line(img, (cx - marker_arm, cy), (cx + marker_arm, cy), color=end_color, thickness=marker_thickness)
        cv2.line(img, (cx, cy - marker_arm), (cx, cy + marker_arm), color=end_color, thickness=marker_thickness)

    # 3) Draw path without obstacles (polyline yellow; single point green)
    path_mask = (path_channel > 0.5).astype(np.uint8) * 255
    if np.any(path_mask):
        try:
            contours, _ = cv2.findContours(path_mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE)
            for cnt in contours:
                if cnt is None or len(cnt) == 0:
                    continue
                if len(cnt) >= 2:
                    cv2.polylines(img, [cnt], isClosed=False, color=path_poly_color, thickness=path_thickness)
                else:
                    x, y = int(cnt[0][0][0]), int(cnt[0][0][1])
                    cv2.circle(img, (x, y), radius=max(1, path_thickness // 2), color=path_point_color, thickness=-1)
        except Exception:
            ys, xs = np.nonzero(path_channel > 0.5)
            for y, x in zip(ys, xs):
                cv2.circle(
                    img, (int(x), int(y)), radius=max(1, path_thickness // 2), color=path_point_color, thickness=-1
                )

    # 4) Draw path with obstacles (alt path) on top
    alt_mask = (alt_path_channel > 0.5).astype(np.uint8) * 255
    if np.any(alt_mask):
        try:
            contours, _ = cv2.findContours(alt_mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE)
            for cnt in contours:
                if cnt is None or len(cnt) == 0:
                    continue
                if len(cnt) >= 2:
                    cv2.polylines(img, [cnt], isClosed=False, color=alt_poly_color, thickness=path_thickness)
                else:
                    x, y = int(cnt[0][0][0]), int(cnt[0][0][1])
                    cv2.circle(img, (x, y), radius=max(1, path_thickness // 2), color=alt_poly_color, thickness=-1)
        except Exception:
            ys, xs = np.nonzero(alt_path_channel > 0.5)
            for y, x in zip(ys, xs):
                cv2.circle(
                    img, (int(x), int(y)), radius=max(1, path_thickness // 2), color=alt_poly_color, thickness=-1
                )

    return img

docs.title: Tensor Format
docs.text:
The core data structure is a 3-channel tensor of shape \((R, R, 3)\) where \(R\) is the resolution:

Channel Name Dtype Range Description 0 Elevation float32 \([0, 1]\) Normalized elevation (\(\bar{e}\)) 1 Markers float32 \(\{-1, 0, 1\}\) Background / start / goal 2 Obstacles float32 \(\{0, 1\}\) Obstacle binary mask

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
Tensors are stored as compressed NumPy arrays:

  1. Tensor is serialized to NumPy .npy format (in memory)
  2. The bytes are compressed with Zstandard at level 12
  3. Saved with the .npy.zst extension
# Encoding (internal)
blob = zstd.compress(numpy_bytes, level=12)

# Decoding (user-facing)
from passage.utils import decode_tensor_blob
tensor = decode_tensor_blob(blob, shape=(256, 256, 3), dtype="float32")

Compression ratio

Typical compression ratios are 3–8× depending on terrain complexity. A 256×256×3 float32 tensor (~768 KB raw) typically compresses to ~100–250 KB.

docs.text: Symbol Definition \(d\) Euclidean distance between adjacent pixels (\(30\,\text{m}\) cardinal, \(30\sqrt{2}\,\text{m}\) diagonal) \(\alpha\) Cost model weight (configurable per solver) \(e(i,j)\) Raw elevation at pixel \((i,j)\) \(\bar{e}(i,j)\) Normalized elevation \(\in [0,1]\) \(\|\bar{e}\|(i,j)\) Absolute normalized elevation \(\Delta e\) Elevation difference \(e_{\text{dst}} - e_{\text{src}}\) \(\Delta e_{\text{range}}\) Global elevation range \(e_{\max} - e_{\min}\)

docs.title: 1. Elevation Cost
docs.text:
Prefer low-elevation pixels. The cost increases proportionally with the destination's normalized elevation:

\[ w_{\text{elevation}} = d \cdot \left(1 + \alpha \cdot \bar{e}_{\text{dst}}\right) \]

When to use

Useful when operating in mountainous terrain where higher altitude = higher risk (weather, oxygen, turbulence). A helicopter might prefer lower valleys.

docs.title: 2. Distance Cost
docs.text:
Pure shortest-path — ignores elevation entirely:

\[ w_{\text{distance}} = d \]

This is the baseline cost model. Combined with A* and a consistent heuristic, it produces geometrically shortest paths.

docs.title: 3. Slope-Uphill Cost
docs.text:
Penalizes uphill movement while treating downhill as free (cost = 0 extra). Models energy expenditure for ground vehicles or the difficulty of gaining altitude:

\[ w_{\text{slope}} = d \cdot \left(1 + \alpha \cdot \frac{\max(0,\; \Delta e)}{\Delta e_{\text{range}}}\right) \]

The \(\max(0, \Delta e)\) term ensures only positive elevation changes (climbing) contribute to the cost. Descending is weighted at the base distance.

Helicopter analogy

A HEMS helicopter climbing from a valley floor to a mountain ridge expends significantly more energy than descending. This model captures that asymmetry.

docs.title: 4. Energy Cost
docs.text:
An additive energy penalty for climbing:

\[ w_{\text{energy}} = d + \alpha \cdot \max(0,\; \Delta e) \]

Unlike the slope model (which is multiplicative), the energy model adds a fixed penalty per meter of elevation gain, independent of horizontal distance.

docs.title: 5. Absolute Cost
docs.text:
Penalizes pixels with high absolute elevation regardless of direction of travel:

\[ w_{\text{absolute}} = d \cdot \left(1 + \alpha \cdot |\bar{e}_{\text{dst}}|\right) \]

This forces paths to stick to regions near sea level, avoiding both mountain peaks and deep depressions.

docs.title: Comparison Table
docs.text: Cost Model Formula Directional? Penalizes Elevation \(d \cdot (1 + \alpha \bar{e}_{\text{dst}})\) No High altitude Distance \(d\) No Long paths only Slope-uphill \(d \cdot (1 + \alpha \cdot \max(0,\Delta e)/\Delta e_{\text{range}})\) Yes (uphill) Climbing Energy \(d + \alpha \cdot \max(0, \Delta e)\) Yes (uphill) Elevation gain Absolute $d \cdot (1 + \alpha \cdot \bar{e}_{\text{dst}} )$

docs.title: Effect of the Weight \(\alpha\)
docs.text:
The weight parameter \(\alpha\) controls the balance between distance and terrain awareness:

  • \(\alpha = 0\): all models reduce to pure distance (shortest path)
  • \(\alpha \gg 1\): terrain features dominate, potentially producing longer but terrain-optimal paths
  • The default weights are calibrated to produce visually distinct paths across cost models
Solver Config Cost Model Default \(\alpha\) astar_elevation Elevation 5,878 astar_energy Energy 3,888 astar_slope Slope-uphill 70,170

Why are weights so large?

Since normalized elevation values are in \([0, 1]\) and pixel distances are \(30\,\text{m}\), large weights are needed to make the terrain component comparable to the distance component. The values were empirically tuned to produce meaningfully different paths.

docs.title: Visual Comparison
docs.text:
On the same terrain and markers, different cost models produce distinctly different paths:

Elevation model → avoids mountain peaks, prefers valleys
Slope model     → avoids steep climbs, may take longer routes
Energy model    → minimizes total elevation gain
Distance model  → straight-line shortest path (baseline)
Absolute model  → stays near sea level

See the Cost Model notebook for interactive visualizations.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
Cost models are implemented in src/passage/pathfinding_utils.py:

  • NetworkX backend: edge weights computed via _compute_edge_weights() using vectorized NumPy operations
  • Grid/Numba backend: step costs computed via _numba_compute_step_cost() — a JIT-compiled function dispatching on cost model ID

Each cost model is identified by a string constant:

COST_MODELS = ["elevation", "distance", "slope_uphill", "energy", "absolute"]

docs.title: Obstacle Generation
docs.text: PASSAGE uses superellipses (Lamé curves) to generate procedural obstacles with rich geometric diversity — from smooth circles to near-rectangular blockers, with arbitrary rotation and size.

docs.title: The Superellipse Equation
docs.text:
A superellipse is defined by the inequality:

\[ \left(\frac{|x - c_x|}{a}\right)^n + \left(\frac{|y - c_y|}{b}\right)^n \leq 1 \]

where:

Parameter Description \((c_x, c_y)\) Center of the obstacle \(a, b\) Semi-axes (horizontal, vertical extent) \(n\) Shape exponent — controls "squareness"

docs.title: Shape Exponent \(n\)
docs.text:
The exponent \(n\) is the key parameter controlling obstacle geometry:

\(n\) value Shape Description \(n = 1\) Diamond (rhombus) Sharp corners, diagonal orientation \(n = 2\) Ellipse Smooth, classical shape \(n = 4\) Rounded rectangle Corners begin to flatten \(n \to \infty\) Rectangle Hard right-angle corners

By default, \(n\) is sampled from a log-uniform distribution:

\[ \log(n) \sim \mathcal{U}(\log(n_{\min}),\; \log(n_{\max})) \]

with \(n_{\min} = 1.0\) and \(n_{\max} = 80.0\). The log-uniform distribution ensures a balanced representation of smooth shapes (\(n \approx 1\text{–}3\)) and angular shapes (\(n \gg 5\)).

Other supported distributions

The obstacles.shape.n.distribution config key also supports:

  • uniform: \(n \sim \mathcal{U}(n_{\min}, n_{\max})\)
  • beta: shaped beta distribution
  • exponential: exponential decay favoring small \(n\)

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
Each obstacle is randomly rotated by an angle \(\theta\) sampled uniformly:

\[ \theta \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 2\pi) \]

The rotation is applied via a standard 2D transformation before the mask is rasterized.

docs.title: Size Parameters
docs.text:
Semi-axes \(a\) and \(b\) are sampled as fractions of the grid resolution \(R\):

\[ a = R \cdot r_a, \quad b = R \cdot r_b \]

where \(r_a, r_b \sim \mathcal{U}(r_{\min}, r_{\max})\) with defaults:

Parameter Default min_ratio 0.02 max_ratio 0.25

This means obstacles range from 2% to 25% of the grid size per axis.

docs.title: Placement Algorithm
docs.text:
Obstacles are placed iteratively until the target coverage ratio is reached:

flowchart TD
    A[Initialize empty mask] --> B{Coverage < ratio_max?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Sample shape params\nn, a, b, θ]
    C --> D[Try up to candidates_per_mask\nrandom positions]
    D --> E{Valid placement?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Rasterize superellipse\nonto mask]
    E -->|No| G[Increment attempt count]
    F --> B
    G --> H{attempts < max_attempts?}
    H -->|Yes| B
    H -->|No| I[Return mask as-is]
    B -->|No| I

    style A fill:#1565C0,color:#fff
    style C fill:#42A5F5,color:#fff
    style F fill:#D32F2F,color:#fff
    style I fill:#2E7D32,color:#fff

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Parameter Default Description ratio_max 0.30 Maximum grid fraction covered by obstacles max_attempts 50 Max placement attempts before stopping candidates_per_mask 200 Positions tested per obstacle obstacle_penalty \(10^8\) Elevation penalty added to blocked cells

docs.title: Obstacle Penalty
docs.text:
When obstacles are applied to the elevation grid for pathfinding, blocked cells receive a massive penalty:

\[ e_{\text{masked}}(i, j) = \max(e) + \text{obstacle\_penalty} \]

This ensures that solvers strongly avoid obstacle regions while still finding valid paths around them (rather than making the graph disconnected).

Note

Paths are computed twice for each solver: once on the free terrain (no obstacles) and once with the obstacle penalty applied. This allows comparing obstacle-free optimal paths with obstacle-aware paths.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The core superellipse mask generation is in src/passage/obstacles.py:

  • superellipse_mask() — rasterizes a single rotated superellipse as a boolean array
  • sample_n_from_config() — samples the exponent from the configured distribution
  • sample_angle_from_config() — samples the rotation angle

The orchestration (multi-obstacle placement loop) lives in src/passage/generate.py:

  • _generate_obstacles_mask() — iterative placement with coverage control

docs.title: Sampling Procedure
docs.text: Each PASSAGE sample is generated through a carefully designed 6-step sampling process. This process ensures geographic diversity, statistical balance across elevation ranges, and consistent normalization.

docs.title: Step 1 — Draw Target Elevation
docs.text:
A target elevation is sampled uniformly from the global calibrated range:

\[ e_{\text{target}} \sim \mathcal{U}(e_{\min}, e_{\max}) \]

where \(e_{\min}\) and \(e_{\max}\) are the global minimum and maximum elevations discovered during the calibration step.

Typical values

With a full global download: \(e_{\min} \approx -415\) m (Dead Sea region), \(e_{\max} \approx 8{,}848\) m (Himalaya).

This uniform sampling ensures that low-altitude coastal regions and high-altitude mountain ranges are represented proportionally across the dataset.

docs.title: Step 2 — Select a Matching Tile
docs.text:
Given \(e_{\text{target}}\), the set of eligible tiles is filtered:

\[ \mathcal{T}_{\text{eligible}} = \left\{ t \in \mathcal{T} \mid e_{\min}^{(t)} \leq e_{\text{target}} \leq e_{\max}^{(t)} \right\} \]

A tile \(t^*\) is then selected uniformly at random from \(\mathcal{T}_{\text{eligible}}\).

Hold-out filtering

If hold-out is enabled, tiles in the hold-out region (e.g., South America) are excluded from training/calibration splits but included in validation/test splits. This ensures geographic generalization can be evaluated.

docs.title: Step 3 — Identify Nearest Pixel
docs.text:
Within the selected tile, the pixel whose elevation is closest to \(e_{\text{target}}\) is identified:

\[ (i^*, j^*) = \arg\min_{(i,j)} \left| e^{(t^*)}(i, j) - e_{\text{target}} \right| \]

This pixel becomes the anchor point around which the crop will be positioned.

docs.title: Step 4 — Extract Random Crop
docs.text:
A crop of size \(R \times R\) (the target resolution) is extracted, with the anchor point positioned randomly within the crop area. The crop origin \((r_0, c_0)\) is computed as:

\[ r_0 = i^* - \delta_r, \quad c_0 = j^* - \delta_c \]

where \(\delta_r \sim \mathcal{U}(0, R-1)\) and \(\delta_c \sim \mathcal{U}(0, R-1)\) are random offsets ensuring the anchor falls somewhere within the crop.

For large resolutions (\(R > 3600\), the JAXA tile size), multiple adjacent tiles are assembled into a grid before cropping:

flowchart LR
    subgraph "2×2 Tile Grid (for 4096×4096)"
        T1["Tile (lat, lon)"] --- T2["Tile (lat, lon+5)"]
        T3["Tile (lat+5, lon)"] --- T4["Tile (lat+5, lon+5)"]
        T1 --- T3
        T2 --- T4
    end
    TG[Assembled Grid<br>7200×7200 px] --> CROP[Random Crop<br>4096×4096 px]

docs.title: Step 5 — Place Start & End Markers
docs.text:
Two marker positions are placed randomly on the crop:

\[ \text{start} = (r_s, c_s), \quad \text{end} = (r_e, c_e) \]

where each coordinate is drawn independently:

\[ r_s, r_e \sim \mathcal{U}(0, R-1), \quad c_s, c_e \sim \mathcal{U}(0, R-1) \]

The marker channel of the output tensor encodes these positions:

Value Meaning \(-1\) Background \(0\) Start marker \(1\) Goal (end) marker

docs.title: Step 6 — Normalize Elevation
docs.text:
The crop's raw elevation values are normalized to \([0, 1]\) using the global calibration bounds:

\[ \bar{e}(i, j) = \frac{e(i, j) - e_{\min}}{e_{\max} - e_{\min}} \]

This ensures that elevation values are directly comparable across samples from different geographic regions.

Denormalization

To recover real elevation in meters from a normalized value:

\[e(i,j) = \bar{e}(i,j) \cdot (e_{\max} - e_{\min}) + e_{\min}\]

The calibration values are stored in calibrate.json and in each sample's metadata.

docs.title: Output Tensor
docs.text:
The final tensor is a 3-channel array of shape \((R, R, 3)\):

Channel Content Range 0 Normalized elevation \(\bar{e}\) \([0, 1]\) 1 Marker map \(\{-1, 0, 1\}\) 2 Obstacle mask \(\{0, 1\}\)

The tensor is compressed with zstandard (level 12) and stored as .npy.zst.

docs.title: Summary Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    E["$e_{target} \\sim \\mathcal{U}(e_{min}, e_{max})$"] --> F[Filter eligible tiles]
    F --> G[Select tile uniformly]
    G --> H[Find nearest pixel]
    H --> I[Extract R×R crop]
    I --> J[Place markers]
    J --> K[Normalize elevation]
    K --> L["Output: (R, R, 3) tensor"]

    style E fill:#1565C0,color:#fff
    style G fill:#42A5F5,color:#fff
    style I fill:#2E7D32,color:#fff
    style L fill:#D32F2F,color:#fff

docs.title: Solvers & Heuristics
docs.text: PASSAGE supports three solver backends and two search algorithms, combined with three admissible heuristics. This modular architecture enables fair comparison of classical pathfinding algorithms on real terrain data.

docs.title: 1. NetworkX Backend
docs.text:
Uses the NetworkX DiGraph with pre-computed edge weights:

  • Pros: Mature library, full-featured, good for moderate grid sizes
  • Cons: Higher memory usage, slower on large grids
  • Graph construction: each pixel is a node; edges connect to 4 or 8 neighbors with weights from the chosen cost model
# Internal: builds a directed graph with weighted edges
graph = build_graph_from_elevation(elevation, weight, diagonal, cost_model)
path = nx.astar_path(graph, start, end, heuristic=h)

docs.title: 2. Pathfinding Backend
docs.text:
Uses the python-pathfinding library:

  • Pros: Purpose-built for grid pathfinding, moderate performance
  • Cons: Node-weighted (not edge-weighted), less flexible cost models
  • Grid construction: a weight matrix is built where each cell contains the cost to enter that cell

docs.title: 3. Grid Backend (Numba-JIT)
docs.text:
PASSAGE's custom implementation — a pure-Python A*/Dijkstra with optional Numba JIT compilation for near-C performance:

  • Pros: Fastest backend, full control over cost model, no external graph library overhead
  • Cons: Requires Numba for best performance (graceful fallback to pure Python)
  • Implementation: binary heap priority queue, inline cost computation, direct array access

Recommended backend

The grid backend is the default and recommended choice. With Numba available, it's the fastest option by a significant margin.

docs.title: A* Search
docs.text:
The classic optimal pathfinding algorithm. Expands nodes by minimizing:

\[ f(s) = g(s) + h(s) \]

where \(g(s)\) is the cost-so-far from start to node \(s\), and \(h(s)\) is the heuristic estimate of the remaining cost to the goal.

Optimality guarantee

With an admissible heuristic (\(h(s) \leq h^*(s)\) for all \(s\)), A* is guaranteed to find the optimal path.

docs.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
docs.text:
Equivalent to A* with \(h(s) = 0\) — explores all directions equally:

\[ f(s) = g(s) \]

Dijkstra always finds the optimal path but explores more nodes than A* with a good heuristic.

docs.title: Heuristics
docs.text: PASSAGE implements three admissible heuristics. All use the physical pixel spacing of \(\Delta = 30\,\text{m}\):

docs.title: Euclidean Heuristic
docs.text:
\[ h_{\text{euclidean}}(s, g) = \Delta \cdot \sqrt{(i_g - i_s)^2 + (j_g - j_s)^2} \]

The straight-line distance. Tightest possible admissible heuristic for grids with diagonal movement.

docs.title: Manhattan Heuristic
docs.text:
\[ h_{\text{manhattan}}(s, g) = \Delta \cdot \left(|i_g - i_s| + |j_g - j_s|\right) \]

Sum of horizontal and vertical distances. Admissible for 4-connected grids (no diagonals).

Warning

Manhattan heuristic overestimates on 8-connected grids (with diagonal movement), making it inadmissible in that setting. Use euclidean or chebyshev instead.

docs.title: Chebyshev Heuristic
docs.text:
\[ h_{\text{chebyshev}}(s, g) = \Delta \cdot \max\left(|i_g - i_s|,\; |j_g - j_s|\right) \]

The "chessboard" distance. Admissible for 8-connected grids and often tighter than Euclidean in practice.

docs.title: Heuristic Comparison
docs.text: Heuristic Formula Best for Tightness Euclidean \(\Delta\sqrt{\Delta i^2 + \Delta j^2}\) 8-connected grids Tightest Manhattan $\Delta( \Delta i + Chebyshev $\Delta \max( \Delta i ,

docs.title: Diagonal Movement
docs.text:
PASSAGE supports three diagonal movement policies:

Policy Description Neighbor count always Diagonal moves always allowed 8 never Only cardinal moves (N/S/E/W) 4 if_at_most_one_obstacle Diagonal allowed unless both adjacent cells are blocked 8 (conditional)

The default configuration uses always with 8-connected movement.

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
Approximate timings for a single path computation on different resolutions (grid backend, Numba-JIT, single core):

Resolution A* (typical) Dijkstra (typical) 64×64 ~1 ms ~2 ms 256×256 ~10 ms ~50 ms 1024×1024 ~200 ms ~2 s 4096×4096 ~5 s ~30 s

Note

Actual timings depend heavily on terrain complexity, obstacle density, and start/end positions. The values above are rough order-of-magnitude estimates.

docs.title: Graph Template Caching
docs.text: For the NetworkX backend, PASSAGE uses a _GraphTemplate class that caches the graph topology (nodes and edge indices) for a given grid shape and connectivity. Only the edge weights are recomputed per sample — avoiding the cost of rebuilding the full graph structure.

docs.title: Numba JIT Compilation
docs.text:
The grid backend's core algorithms (_numba_astar_core, _numba_dijkstra_core) are decorated with @numba.njit:

  • First call triggers JIT compilation (~2-5 seconds)
  • Subsequent calls run at native speed
  • Graceful fallback to pure Python if Numba is not installed

docs.title: Path Cost Computation
docs.text:
After a path is found, its total cost is computed by summing edge weights along the path:

\[ C(\text{path}) = \sum_{k=0}^{|\text{path}|-2} w(p_k, p_{k+1}) \]

This cost is stored in the sample metadata alongside the path coordinates and solver timing information.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PASSAGE follows a linear, four-step pipeline. Each step is a CLI subcommand that can be run independently, supports resume, and produces well-defined outputs:

docs.title: Step 2 — Calibrate Elevations
docs.text: The calibration step scans all downloaded tiles to compute global minimum and maximum elevation values. These statistics are essential for the generation step, which normalizes elevation data into the [0, 1] range.

docs.title: Why Calibrate?
docs.text:
Each JAXA tile contains raw elevation values in meters. To create consistent, comparable samples across resolutions and geographic regions, PASSAGE normalizes elevation using global bounds:

\[ \bar{e}(i,j) = \frac{e(i,j) - e_{\min}}{e_{\max} - e_{\min}} \]

Where \(e_{\min}\) and \(e_{\max}\) are the global minimum and maximum across all tiles — determined by this calibration step.
